_notes: Coefficients set relative importance only; direction comes from higher_is_better. Each metric's improvement over the stored reference (scoring/scores_test.json, method spmc_frs) is normalised by its spread across ranked attempts.

No metric depends on wall-clock time. The paper's speed claim (< 1 s per case, O(n)) is enforced as a constraint instead: the evaluator caps every method at 1 CPU-second per instance (kernel-measured, ~20x the reference); exceeding it fails the run.
A failed run (crash, invalid/non-SO(3) output, import failure, CPU budget overrun) receives the worst value of every metric: 180 deg for error metrics, 0 for success rates.

results.*: numbers transcribed by earlier iterations. The paper prints per-(pattern, config) box-plot medians in Fig. 4 and the textual claims listed under _paper_reported_unscored; the aggregate robust-alignment values below are earlier approximations of those figures and are kept unchanged. sparse_alignment has no paper counterpart: its results are this gym's measured reference (hidden test).

Image experiments use a public world-map substitute (the paper's image is unreleased) with synthetic clutter at the paper's five clutter levels, so the paper's 0.89/1.32/2.96 deg values are indicative, not same-setup targets.

fig4_A1_medians_deg._order: B1..B7; read from the printed box-plot medians of Fig. 4 (Dataset A1)

robust_alignment_all.description: Paper Experiment 1 (Sec. 5.1 / 9.1): 5 template patterns A1-A5 x 7 source configurations B1-B7 (none; 0.01 noise; +10/25/50/75/90% uniform outliers) x 100 uniformly random rotations = 3,500 registrations. Hidden test: fresh secret noise/outlier realisations and rotations of the same protocol. Errors are geodesic rotation errors in degrees.

success_rate_1deg.description: Fraction of registrations with error <= 1 deg.

robust_alignment_high_outliers.description: The B5-B7 subset (50/75/90% added outliers) of robust_alignment_all: 1,500 registrations. The paper's robustness claim: the hybrid stays accurate where SPMC's mean alignment degrades.

success_rate_1deg.description: Fraction of high-outlier registrations with error <= 1 deg.

spherical_image_alignment_all.description: Paper Experiment 3 (Sec. 5.3): a 360x180 world-map image (public GeoJSON substitute) is the template; sources add clutter at 0/5/10/15/19.3% of the sphere, are rotated and re-rasterised; both images become point sets via SphImg2SphPoints (intensity threshold 0.21, done by the evaluator). 5 clutter levels x 100 rotations = 500 registrations.

success_rate_1deg.description: Fraction of image registrations with error <= 1 deg.

spherical_image_alignment_high_clutter.description: The hardest image setting (Img5, about 19.3% clutter) of spherical_image_alignment_all: 100 registrations; typical and worst-case error.

sparse_alignment.description: Where the paper's method falls short (the low-density end of its Fig. 6 study, 10^3 points): template and source are INDEPENDENT 1,000- or 3,000-point samples of the same pattern (no shared points), source with 0.01 noise and 10% uniform outliers. 5 patterns x 2 sizes x 50 rotations = 500 registrations. No paper numbers exist; results are this gym's measured reference.

success_rate_5deg.description: Fraction of sparse registrations with error <= 5 deg (not grossly failed).
